fluff.overview: The Demon series of battle armor emerged from Gibson Federated BattleMechs during the Jihad as the companion line to the Word of Blake's Celestial OmniMechs. Conceived by Precentor Vapula, the Manei Domini's engineering chief, the six Demon designs draw their names from the malevolent figures of various world mythologies. Each suit was crafted to fill a specific combat role while projecting an element of psychological terror against the Word's enemies. Fielded almost exclusively by the cybernetically enhanced Manei Domini elite, the Demons share the same unsettling visual aesthetic as their larger Celestial counterparts and were rarely encountered outside the Shadow Divisions.
fluff.capabilities: The standard Nephilim focuses its firepower around a man-portable plasma rifle in a modular right-arm mount, supplemented by twin SRM-2 launchers over the shoulders. This combination provides both sustained energy fire and a missile barrage capable of threatening armored vehicles and BattleMechs. The suit's 850 kilograms of mimetic armor can absorb two large laser hits while actively distorting the trooper's visual signature to interfere with enemy targeting. Enhanced ground speed compensates for the lack of jump capability. As an assault-class design massing a full two tons, the Nephilim is too heavy for OmniMech transport and cannot conduct swarming attacks. Its role is that of a ground-based heavy weapons platform, relying on armor and firepower to dominate engagements rather than mobility and stealth.
fluff.deployment: Clan forces that engaged Nephilim troopers during the Jihad faced one of the most formidable battlesuits in existence. Any salvaged examples organized into five-trooper Points would have represented a significant intelligence prize, though the suit's two-ton mass and Inner Sphere technology base made integration into Clan formations impractical for sustained use.
fluff.history:
Alongside its counterpart the Shedu, the Nephilim rounded out the Demon series with its entry into the assault class. Debuting last in the entire line, the Nephilim's first recorded appearance came during fighting on Gibson in mid-3071. Even at that early stage, the suit's powerful build, thick sensor-defeating armor, and range of equipment configurations quickly identified it as perhaps the pinnacle of Vapula's creations.

The Nephilim was the Demon that came closest to fulfilling Vapula's original vision for the entire program. Stealthy, mobile, and well armored, its generous use of modular and detachable weapons emphasized a flexibility that the other Demons only dabbled in. Where the Tengu had been the experimental proof of concept for Celestial-like adaptability in battle armor, the Nephilim was the refined production model. Six basic configurations were identified over the course of the Jihad, and the suit's modular nature spawned an even wider variety of one-off field variants observed in engagements across the Inner Sphere. Opposing commanders learned to tell their troops only that they could expect missile or rocket fire from suits shrouded in heavy sensor-defeating armor, because predicting the specific loadout of any given Nephilim formation was essentially impossible.

Even the suit's name reinforced the connection to the Celestials. Taken from Christian legends of half-angels who lived among humanity, the designation hinted at the Nephilim's closer relation to the Celestial OmniMechs than any other Demon design, and likely at the engineering goals Vapula had aimed for when developing the entire series. If the Celestials were the angels of the Word's arsenal, the Nephilim was the bridge between those divine machines and the infernal battlesuits that fought at their feet.

Despite its capabilities, the Nephilim had one of the lowest distribution rates in the entire Demon series. As the most recently introduced design, production time had been limited, and the suit never appeared in the ranks of the regular Word of Blake Militia or Protectorate Militia. Even the Shadow Divisions lacked widespread access. Allied intelligence placed the largest confirmed concentrations in the Forty-fourth, Forty-seventh, Forty-ninth, and Fifty-second Shadow Divisions only. Commanders who faced the Nephilim in battle quickly discovered that the suits were too formidable for most other battle armor to contend with. Medium-weight combat vehicles and BattleMechs were considered the most effective means of countering these assault-class Demons.
